The item reads "...Berzin; RY/Waldo/Valby via Tsadra permission." docs/research/STEINERT_DICT_LICENSES.md never mentions Tsadra (grep: no match). docs/DICTIONARY_STRATEGY.md:79 still lists "RY/Waldo/Valby via Tsadra (queued)" as a pending build-order step, and :46-48 spells out what verification means here: "Hopkins (UMA's stated distribution terms), ITLR and TibTermProject (check terms), Rangjung Yeshe / Waldo / Valby (permission via Tsadra, already on the survey list)." 2) The claim's load-bearing mitigation — "None of them appears under data/ or data/extracted/" — is factually false. data/extracted/thl_dicts.jsonl (58MB, present in the tree) carries exactly these dictionaries under their THL codes: IW 128,652 entries (Ives Waldo), RY 80,104 (Rangjung Yeshe), JV 67,669 (Jim Valby), DM 20,679 (Dan Martin), RB 5,128 (Richard Barron), and the Hopkins family JH-ENG 17,186 / JH-SKT 15,548 / JH-OE 6,841 / JH-T 5,005 / JH-C 2,191 plus nine more JH-* codes. 3) The two distribution documents the claim cites as cover say the opposite in their own words. docs/distribution/OPEN_SOURCE_NOTICES.md:117, on the "THL dictionary payload (Waldo, Rangjung Yeshe, Valby, Dan Martin, Hopkins layers, etc.)": "per-dictionary terms, **licensing review still pending**" — the exact review this item asks for, recorded as pending. docs/distribution/PAYLOAD_MANIFEST.txt:128-129 labels both extractions "terms unreviewed". On the verification itself: STEINERT_DICT_LICENSES.md disposes of Hopkins/UMA, ITLR and Berzin by naming them inside one bulk paragraph headed "Not redistributable without permission", citing no terms text for any of them. For ITLR it writes "(collaborative project, own terms)" — an admission the terms were noted to exist, not read. The item asks specifically for UMA's stated distribution terms and ITLR's terms; neither is quoted or linked. Only TibTermProject gets a real disposition (move to outreach, ask CTA Dept of Education), and that ask is queued, not sent.

CLASSIFICATION: section "adam" — closing the item needs asks that go out in Adam's name (Tsadra permission for RY/Waldo/Valby; CTA DoE for TibTermProject), though the desk half (reading and citing UMA's, ITLR's and Berzin's published terms, then correcting OPEN_SOURCE_NOTICES.md:117) needs nobody. blocking: false — market DMGs already strip the unreviewed payload under an enforced gate, so 1.0 can ship; the exposure is team builds only. effort: small. summary: "Verify the Steinert dictionaries' licences one by one — Hopkins/UMA, ITLR, TibTermProject, Berzin — and pursue RY/Waldo/Valby via Tsadra."

REFUTED — the item is open. TODO.md:3223 is still `- [ ]`, and three parts of the ask are unmet in the tree as it stands.

1) THE GATE IS VACUOUS, AND ITS OWN INVARIANT IS ALREADY VIOLATED. app/main.cpp:19651 computes `const bool inAbout = QString(kDefectIntake).contains('@');` — it never inspects the About dialog. Worse, the invariant it claims to pin is FALSE right now: there are TWO hardcoded copies of the address — `kDefectIntake` at app/main.cpp:961 and a raw `"mailto:adam.derick.andrade@gmail.com?subject="` at app/main.cpp:48568 (Help ▸ Troubleshooting ▸ Report a Problem…), which does not use the constant. The gate cannot see the second copy. A test that passes while the thing it names is untrue is not evidence of done.

2) A SECOND, UNREDACTED DIAGNOSTIC REPORT SHIPS IN THE SAME MENU AND LEAKS EXACTLY WHAT THE REDACTION EXISTS TO HIDE. Help ▸ Troubleshooting (created unconditionally at app/main.cpp:48424) carries "Generate Diagnostic Report…" (48538) built by a local lambda at app/main.cpp:48483-48536 — NOT `buildDiagnosticReport` (app/textreport.h:55). That lambda writes `installInfo()` (which interpolates `root`, a path under the user's home → the user's name), `QCoreApplication::applicationFilePath()`, the lifecycle log's last 60 lines, and a loop over `QSettings::allKeys()` printing every key and value — which includes `scan/recent`, the full paths of recently opened texts, read at app/main.cpp:48118. The redacted report's whole stated rationale (app/textreport.h:39-52: "the title of a text can itself be the sensitive part... the home directory carries the user's name") is bypassed by a sibling menu item, and the selftest pins only the redacted one.

3) THE PLAN'S LITERAL ASK IS HALF-MET, AND ITS ADAM-OWNED HALF IS UNRULED. docs/RELEASE_PLAN_2026-09.md:83-84 asks for the address "printed in About **and in Help → Save Diagnostic Report**". About does print it (app/main.cpp:47857-47863), but `buildDiagnosticReport` (app/textreport.h:55-81) contains no address at all — a user who saves the report has a file with nothing in it saying where to send it. And the address itself is Adam's/ALL's ruling, not mine: docs/RELEASE_PLAN_2026-09.md:202 lists "Defect-intake address" as decision #5 Adam owns; docs/RISK_REGISTER.md:201 records the "defect-intake alias" as owner: ALL. CLASSIFICATION — section: blocking-adam · blocking: true · effort: small · summary: "A ruled defect-intake address, printed in About and in the saved report, one copy, no unredacted twin."

To close it: get Adam's ruling on the address (alias or GitHub Issues), collapse app/main.cpp:48568 onto `kDefectIntake`, decide between the two Help report paths and make the survivor use the redacted builder, print the address inside the saved report, and replace the vacuous `inAbout` with a check that actually reads the About dialog's text and greps the binary's sources for stray copies.
